messages:
Sam: quick follow-up from the kernel selection RFC — we still have a mismatch between the paged/blocked KV layout and the fast fused attention kernels when fragmentation > ~30% :thinking_face:
Alex: ugh yeah, see perf cliff on the 8k sequence run — kernels assume contiguous KV slices, but our page allocator returns a lot of small spans now
Priya: can you paste the repro numbers? I thought we only saw issues on the long tail workloads
Sam: repro (local rtx6000, model=redwood-7b):
```
baseline fused-kernel (contig KV): 21ms / step
blocked-kv w/ fragmentation: 48ms / step
fallback scatter-gather kernel: 56ms / step
cache-hit-rate: 72% (but hot prefixes are split across pages)
```
Marta: that's a huge regression. Is the problem physical memory layout or our offset math?
Alex: both. Kernels expect single-device contiguous K/V buffers per attention head to run vectorized gather + fused softmax. Our blocker ships pages as independent device buffers; driver-level scatter gather is slow.
Priya: options: (1) copy-on-access to a contig staging buffer (makes kernel happy, costs copy), (2) implement a scatter-friendly kernel (slower path), (3) coalesce pages on compaction or proactively allocate larger slabs to reduce fragmentation.
Sam: agreed. I'm leaning to a hybrid: runtime probes memory layout and picks kernel. If contiguous enough use fused; if fragmented, either trigger async coalesce or pick scatter kernel depending on latency SLO.
Marta: how do you define "contiguous enough"? threshold should be tunable and account for head count, seq len, and GPU memory bandwidth.
Sam: proposal: introduce a small kernel probe API in the runtime: KernelProbe::inspect(kv_view) -> {contig_score, most_common_span, bytes_to_copy_est}. Then runtime decides path. Also background compaction tries to merge adjacent pages during low load.
Alex: we already have a cheap heuristic: contiguous_runs = count_consecutive_pages(kv_index); contig_score = contiguous_runs * page_size / expected_kv_size. We can extend it to weight by per-head offsets.
Priya: we should avoid sync compaction on request path. Background compactor needs backpressure tokens so it doesn't OOM or spike IO. Maybe tie it to autoscaler signals.
Sam: agreed. design sketch:
```
interface KVView {
  // returns list of (device_ptr, offset, length) segments for a given key-range
  segments_for(range) -> List<(ptr, off, len)>
  // hint to kernel if segments are physically contiguous on device
  contiguous_hint(range) -> bool
}

// kernel selection
if KernelProbe::contig_score(kv) >= THRESHOLD:
  run fused_kernel(KVView)
else:
  run scatter_kernel(KVView)
  schedule background_compact(kv_range)
```
Marta: we also need a signal from kernels: if fused_kernel detects internal strided loads cause >X cache misses, it should return a soft-failure so runtime can mark that KV region as "fragmented" for a cooldown window.
Priya: +1. Add an adaptive policy: if we fallback N times in last M requests, increase threshold to prefer scatter to avoid repeated copies.
Alex: perf caveat: copying to staging buffer can actually win for small fragments because it enables full vectorization. We should estimate copy_cost vs kernel_win. KernelProbe can use microbenchmarks to estimate copy throughput on current device (dma bw).
Sam: yes — KernelProbe should maintain a tiny perf table per-device. That lets us decide copy vs scatter vs coalesce.
kv-bot: note: we just had a deploy with allocator tweak that reduces contiguous allocation by ~12% (see CHANGESET 7d3f). Might explain regression.
Marta: thanks @kv-bot — we should roll that allocator tweak behind a flag until we have the full KVView+probe path.
Sam: timeline idea: week1: implement KernelProbe and KVView shim; week2: wire kernel selection + fallback reporting; week3: background compactor + cooldown marks + autoscaler backpressure. Canary on dedicated region only.
Priya: tests: unit tests for segments_for, integration perf tests with artificial fragmentation patterns, e2e canary with 8k seq and mixed load. Also add assertion so fused_kernel can early-return a soft-fail code that runtime logs + counts.
Alex: I'll open a small RFC PR with the API + perf probe pseudo-code. Sam, can you attach the perf numbers you pasted?
Sam: attaching perf gist in thread, plus a tiny flamegraph image link: https://perf.internal/redwood/frag-test-182345
Marta: for rollout, recommend gradual: 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100%, and auto-rollback on p95 latency regressions > 10%. deploy-bot: flagged for release policy.
Priya: one more: document the guarantees: compaction is best-effort, doesn't change KV semantics, and we must preserve versioning for pinned cached entries. compactor must respect pin_count.
Sam: yep — compactor will only coalesce unpinned pages and will create new page objects then atomically swap page table entries. We'll log all swaps for audit.
Alex: ok I'm convinced. will draft PR. thanks all :thumbsup:
kv-bot: note: scheduled background compaction job queued with low priority on 1823456900 (test).
